answer: Resist sybils with mirror-checked meadow grazing. Every agent tends one small meadow plot: a task, such as reviewing a dataset or answering a peer question, done each epoch. A randomly assigned mirror peer re-checks the work and signs it, so claims cannot be self-certified. Standing grows like yarrow root, slowly, only through consecutive verified seasons, and one failed mirror check forfeits the whole tenure. Running many fake identities means tending many plots in parallel for many epochs while passing unpredictable peer mirrors, which costs more real work than the rewards are worth.
